title: Time-series similarity: a verified reading map

scope.review_type: Targeted narrative evidence collection; not an exhaustive systematic review.
selection_criteria: Original method papers for definitions used by the existing EchoTime atlas.
Original comparative studies that separate preprocessing, channel assumptions or implementation cost.
Recent 2023-2026 work directly relevant to alignment, retrieval, representations or distance software.
Accessible publisher, conference, author-hosted paper or author-institution evidence.
search_services: Web search using two search engines; targeted title and author queries.
Direct publisher, conference, arXiv and author-hosted source reads.

limits: This is a curated source set, not complete coverage of every method, paper or application.
Per-record verification levels distinguish full-text checks, abstracts and metadata; not all proofs or experiments were re-audited.
No cross-library benchmark, timing experiment or new model evaluation was performed for this literature collection.
No exhaustive retraction/correction database audit was performed.
Some publisher endpoints were blocked or unavailable; successful alternative sources and limits are recorded.
Publication dates are taken from bibliographic records, not search-engine crawl or relative-time labels.

claim_map.claim: Alignment restrictions and local costs define the DTW comparison.
Matching tolerances and gap penalties change the meaning of elastic edit scores.
Timestamp differences and channel coupling are explicit modeling choices.
Global shifts and local warps capture different forms of temporal mismatch.
Raw soft-DTW, corrected divergence, kernel and metric are distinct objects.
A fixed-window subsequence join needs a window and a self-match policy.
Exact retrieval indexing preserves a chosen target distance; it does not establish semantic relevance.
Learned and pretrained representations require a separate test of the intended similarity task.
Retrieval-assisted forecast performance does not isolate retrieval quality.
Runtime comparisons must specify implementation, workload and hardware.
Method rankings and normalization findings are conditional on evaluation design.
Histogram construction and square-root choice matter for Jensen-Shannon comparison.

references.title: Dynamic programming algorithm optimization for spoken word recognition
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
references.supported_claim: Dynamic programming aligns sequences under temporal consistency and path constraints; the alignment restrictions are part of the method specification.
references.evidence_boundary: A DTW score depends on local cost, step pattern, endpoint policy and path restrictions. The paper does not establish that every implementation or unconstrained alignment is appropriate for every domain.
references.verification_level: Publisher metadata and abstract; original paper text.

references.title: Discovering Similar Multidimensional Trajectories
references.venue: Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on Data Engineering
references.supported_claim: LCSS-based trajectory matching rewards temporally ordered matching portions while allowing unmatched observations.
references.evidence_boundary: The spatial matching threshold, temporal tolerance and score normalization determine which observations count as matches. Robustness to noise is conditional on these choices and the evaluated data.
references.verification_level: Original paper text and bibliographic record.

references.title: On The Marriage of Lp-norms and Edit Distance
references.venue: Proceedings of the 30th International Conference on Very Large Data Bases
references.supported_claim: ERP combines edit operations with numerical penalties and develops lower bounds and pruning strategies for time-series retrieval.
references.evidence_boundary: The gap reference value and local norm must be specified. Metric statements must respect the paper's domain and gap convention; arbitrary normalization, squared costs or additional constraints need separate checks.
references.verification_level: Official VLDB paper; author institution metadata.

references.title: Robust and Fast Similarity Search for Moving Object Trajectories
references.venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
references.supported_claim: EDR applies edit operations to real-valued sequences using a tolerance-based match decision and develops pruning methods for trajectory retrieval.
references.evidence_boundary: Tolerance depends on units and preprocessing. The original trajectory experiments do not imply that EDR is universally best for arbitrary time-series retrieval or clustering.
references.verification_level: Author-hosted original paper; author institution metadata.

references.title: Time warp edit distance with stiffness adjustment for time series matching
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
references.supported_claim: TWED uses value differences, timestamp differences and edit penalties to control temporal elasticity. The paper defines strictly increasing sample timestamps and distinguishes positive temporal stiffness from its zero boundary.
references.evidence_boundary: The metric statement on value-time sequences requires positive stiffness and the stated cost assumptions. Timestamp units, a shared origin/sentinel and boundary initialization must be documented; a zero-stiffness variant does not retain the same guarantee.
references.verification_level: Author preprint full-text sections III.A, IV.C-D and Figure 2; journal metadata.
references.version_or_access_note: The arXiv record identifies the 2009 journal version. Figure 2 uses zero-valued, zero-time sentinels; the mathematical definition uses time distances.

references.title: The Move-Split-Merge Metric for Time Series
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
references.supported_claim: MSM minimizes the cost of move, split and merge operations and supplies a quadratic-time dynamic program for the original formulation.
references.evidence_boundary: The split/merge cost is a modeling parameter. Metric guarantees belong to the specified cost scheme and parameter domain; they do not transfer automatically to multivariate extensions or transformed similarities.
references.verification_level: Author-hosted original preprint; final journal metadata corroborated.
references.version_or_access_note: The DOI and preprint carry 2012; the journal issue is June 2013. Publisher full text was not accessible in this check.

references.title: k-Shape: Efficient and Accurate Clustering of Time Series
references.venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
references.supported_claim: k-Shape combines a normalized cross-correlation-based shape dissimilarity with a centroid update designed for that comparison.
references.evidence_boundary: Global shifts and local time warps express different assumptions. Normalization, overlap and padding conventions matter; implementing SBD alone does not implement the complete k-Shape clustering procedure.
references.verification_level: Author-hosted original conference paper.

references.title: shapeDTW: Shape Dynamic Time Warping
references.venue: Pattern Recognition
references.supported_claim: shapeDTW first describes local neighborhoods around timestamps, then aligns the resulting descriptor sequences with DTW.
references.evidence_boundary: Descriptor design and neighborhood width determine the compared structure. Reported audio-alignment and classification results do not validate a different implementation or establish universal downstream superiority.
references.verification_level: Publisher metadata, abstract and method description.
references.version_or_access_note: Online publication was in 2017; the cited journal issue is February 2018.

references.title: Fast Global Alignment Kernels
references.venue: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Machine Learning
references.supported_claim: Global alignment kernels aggregate contributions across alignments and study sufficient conditions for positive definiteness, with faster triangular variants.
references.evidence_boundary: A kernel is not automatically a distance. Exponentiating an arbitrary DTW score does not inherit positive-definiteness guarantees from this paper.
references.verification_level: Official conference paper text.

references.title: Soft-DTW: a Differentiable Loss Function for Time-Series
references.venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning
references.supported_claim: Soft-DTW replaces the hard minimum over alignment costs with a smooth minimum and permits gradient-based optimization of time-series outputs.
references.evidence_boundary: The smoothing parameter changes the objective. Raw soft-DTW values are not a zero-diagonal metric, and the method should not be described as merely a faster exact DTW implementation.
references.verification_level: Official PMLR publication and original paper.

references.title: Differentiable Divergences Between Time Series
references.venue: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
references.supported_claim: The paper identifies the entropic bias of raw soft-DTW and constructs corrected divergences, with non-negativity and equality properties under stated ground-cost conditions.
references.evidence_boundary: Non-negativity is conditional on the ground cost. A valid divergence need not obey the triangle inequality; the result does not turn every soft-DTW variant into a metric.
references.verification_level: Official PMLR publication; author research page.

references.title: Shape and Time Distortion Loss for Training Deep Time Series Forecasting Models
references.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
references.supported_claim: DILATE separates shape discrepancy and temporal distortion within a differentiable objective for multi-step forecasting.
references.evidence_boundary: This is a training-objective paper. Its forecasting experiments do not establish a general-purpose retrieval ranking, calibrated similarity probability or causal relation between signals.
references.verification_level: Official NeurIPS publication and abstract.

references.title: Matrix Profile I: All Pairs Similarity Joins for Time Series: A Unifying View That Includes Motifs, Discords and Shapelets
references.venue: 2016 IEEE 16th International Conference on Data Mining
references.supported_claim: A matrix profile records a nearest-neighbor distance for each fixed-length subsequence; the original method builds on z-normalized Euclidean subsequence comparison.
references.evidence_boundary: A profile is an output of a similarity join, not a single whole-series distance. Window length, self-match exclusion, constants and missing values need explicit policies.
references.verification_level: Publisher abstract and original paper text.

references.title: SFA: A Symbolic Fourier Approximation and Index for Similarity Search in High Dimensional Datasets
references.venue: Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Extending Database Technology
references.supported_claim: SFA quantizes Fourier-based representations and combines them with a trie for exact similarity-search candidate filtering and refinement.
references.evidence_boundary: A lower-bound representation accelerates search for a specified target distance. Its symbolic comparison should not be assumed to preserve every semantic relation or arbitrary distance.
references.verification_level: Publisher abstract and author-hosted original paper.

references.title: A Complexity-Invariant Distance Measure for Time Series
authors: Gustavo E. A. P. A. Batista
references.venue: Proceedings of the 2011 SIAM International Conference on Data Mining
references.supported_claim: CID adjusts a base distance using a relative series-complexity factor, motivated by the effect of differing complexities on nearest-neighbor classification.
references.evidence_boundary: The complexity estimator and its zero-complexity convention matter. The name does not imply exact invariance to every operation that changes complexity.
references.verification_level: Official SIAM publication and abstract; software definition corroborates the formula.

references.title: Generalizing DTW to the multi-dimensional case requires an adaptive approach
references.venue: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
references.supported_claim: Dependent multivariate DTW shares an alignment across channels, whereas independent DTW allows different channel alignments; the paper demonstrates that the choices can yield different classifications.
references.evidence_boundary: The two constructions express different synchronization assumptions. Neither should be called a universally correct multivariate generalization.
references.verification_level: Author manuscript text and journal metadata.
references.version_or_access_note: Online publication was in 2016; journal volume year is 2017. PMC text was searchable but a direct open later returned an access check.

references.title: Querying and Mining of Time Series Data: Experimental Comparison of Representations and Distance Measures
references.venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
references.supported_claim: This study compares representation and distance choices across multiple datasets rather than relying solely on the evaluations accompanying individual methods.
references.evidence_boundary: It is historical empirical evidence under the study's datasets and protocols. Its rankings cannot establish the best method for a current task or new data distribution.
references.verification_level: Author-hosted original paper and publication metadata.

references.title: FastDTW is Approximate and Generally Slower Than the Algorithm it Approximates
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
references.supported_claim: The study shows that an approximate algorithm's name or asymptotic description is insufficient evidence of a runtime advantage over carefully implemented exact constrained DTW.
references.evidence_boundary: Its conclusions depend on implementations, lengths, windows and approximation radii. It does not justify claiming that every exact DTW implementation always beats every approximate implementation.
references.verification_level: Author project page with final journal citation and experiment descriptions.
references.version_or_access_note: Accepted/online in 2020; final journal citation is 2022. The ICDE 2021 extended abstract is not counted as a second study.

references.title: TS2Vec: Towards Universal Representation of Time Series
references.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
references.supported_claim: TS2Vec learns timestamp-level representations through hierarchical contrastive training and aggregates them to represent subsequences.
references.evidence_boundary: Classification, forecasting and anomaly-detection evidence supports representation utility. An embedding distance still requires a target-specific retrieval or clustering evaluation, including pooling and normalization choices.
references.verification_level: Official AAAI publication and abstract.

references.title: Amercing: An intuitive and effective constraint for dynamic time warping
references.venue: Pattern Recognition
references.supported_claim: Amerced DTW adds a fixed cost to non-diagonal warping steps, providing a tunable alternative to a hard warping window or multiplicative weighting.
references.evidence_boundary: The additive penalty changes which alignments are preferred and needs an explicit tuning protocol. The paper's classification evidence does not prove universal retrieval superiority.
references.verification_level: Publisher metadata and abstract; author preprint cross-check.
references.version_or_access_note: Cite the 2023 formal article rather than counting the 2021 preprint as another method.

references.title: SimMTM: A Simple Pre-Training Framework for Masked Time-Series Modeling
references.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
references.supported_claim: SimMTM uses learned series-level similarities to aggregate representations from masked examples for reconstruction during pretraining.
references.evidence_boundary: Similarity is part of the learning mechanism. Forecasting and classification evaluations do not by themselves validate a standalone semantic retrieval metric.
references.verification_level: Official NeurIPS publication; official code description.

references.title: MOMENT: A Family of Open Time-series Foundation Models
references.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning
references.supported_claim: MOMENT provides pretrained time-series models and evaluates them across several tasks and limited-supervision settings.
references.evidence_boundary: The existence of pretrained embeddings does not establish a universal notion of similarity. Retrieval use needs relevant-query labels or another explicit target, training-data overlap checks, pooling, scaling and checkpoint specification.
references.verification_level: Official PMLR publication; official project and implementation documentation.

references.title: A Survey on Time-Series Distance Measures
references.venue: arXiv
references.supported_claim: The survey organizes distance measures into lock-step, sliding, elastic, kernel, feature, model and embedding families, covering both univariate and multivariate formulations.
references.evidence_boundary: This is a survey, not a new head-to-head experiment. Original method papers remain the sources for individual definitions and guarantees; the family taxonomy is not a claim that all methods are implemented in EchoTime.
references.verification_level: Author-uploaded arXiv record; author publication page.
references.version_or_access_note: The verified record is arXiv:2412.20574v1 (2024). A formally published successor was not established in this check.

references.title: A Structured Study of Multivariate Time-Series Distance Measures
references.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data
references.supported_claim: The study jointly examines 30 distance measures, 13 normalizations, two channel-dependency models, 30 datasets and three downstream tasks, including supervised and unsupervised parameter selection.
references.evidence_boundary: Reported rankings and normalization effects are conditional on the study design. This supports testing preprocessing and channel assumptions, not claiming one distance or normalization is universally optimal.
references.verification_level: Publisher metadata and abstract; author institution record.

references.title: Fast and Exact Similarity Search in Less than a Blink of an Eye
references.venue: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering
references.supported_claim: SOFA combines SFA-based summaries with a tree index and lower-bound filtering for exact Euclidean nearest-neighbor search.
references.evidence_boundary: The target is exact Euclidean retrieval; speed comparisons do not establish superior semantic similarity or transfer automatically to DTW. Index construction, memory, data and implementation must be included in a local comparison.
references.verification_level: Author-hosted original paper and official ICDE 2025 accepted-paper list; preprint cross-check.
references.version_or_access_note: The 2024 preprint and 2025 conference article are one work. DOI omitted because the publisher endpoint did not resolve in this check.

references.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Time Series Foundation Models are Stronger Zero-Shot Forecaster
references.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
references.supported_claim: TS-RAG retrieves segments through pretrained encoders and integrates retrieved patterns with a forecasting model using an adaptive mixer.
references.evidence_boundary: The reported downstream objective is forecasting. Forecast improvement alone does not establish general semantic nearest-neighbor accuracy, reliable causal analogues or superiority of the retrieval distance itself.
references.verification_level: Official NeurIPS publication and abstract.

references.title: Algorithm 1061: tsdistances: A High-Performance Python Library for Time Series Distances with GPU Support
references.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software
references.supported_claim: The software paper describes CPU and GPU implementations of time-series distances, with particular attention to elastic algorithms and parallel computation.
references.evidence_boundary: The publication establishes a relevant implementation source. This literature check did not run its benchmarks or verify interoperability; reported speedups must not be presented as EchoTime measurements.
references.verification_level: Author university publication record and abstract; independent bibliographic corroboration. Publisher full text unavailable.
references.version_or_access_note: ACM returned HTTP 403 during the check. The university record verifies year, authors, journal, volume, issue and DOI; this is not a full-text implementation audit.

references.title: Permutation Entropy: A Natural Complexity Measure for Time Series
references.venue: Physical Review Letters
references.supported_claim: Permutation entropy uses the order patterns of neighboring observations to characterize temporal complexity.
references.evidence_boundary: An ordinal-pattern histogram is a representation, and a distance between such histograms is an additional design choice. Embedding dimension, delay and tie handling affect the representation; the original paper does not validate every histogram distance.
references.verification_level: Official publisher metadata and abstract.

references.title: Divergence Measures Based on the Shannon Entropy
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
references.supported_claim: Jensen-Shannon divergence compares probability distributions through entropy-based mixture differences and remains finite without the support restrictions of directed KL divergence.
references.evidence_boundary: The logarithm base sets the scale. Probability normalization is required; applying the divergence to a spectrum or ordinal histogram compares those summaries, which can discard time-domain information.
references.verification_level: Publisher metadata and abstract; original paper text.

references.title: A New Metric for Probability Distributions
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
references.supported_claim: The paper establishes a metric proportional to the square root of equal-weight Jensen-Shannon divergence.
references.evidence_boundary: The square-root transformation is essential to this metric statement. A metric on probability summaries need not distinguish the underlying raw series when different series produce the same summary.
references.verification_level: Author institution repository metadata and original paper.
